LESSON: WRITING 13.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Writing 13.4.1 Spelling

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 13.4.1 Spelling. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we write words correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly
2. spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly
3. uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 13.4.1 SPELLING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 13.4.1 Spelling helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 13.4.1 SPELLING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.4.1 Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.4.1 Spelling to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 13.4.1 Spelling is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.4.1 Spelling”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.4.1 Spelling to a partner. (skill: spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 13.4.1 Spelling to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
3. Practise this skill: spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
4. Practise this skill: uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 13.4.1 Spelling from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 13.4.1 Spelling: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 13.4.1 Spelling?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we write words correctly?
2. Which words have the same pronunciation but different spelling?
3. what went well and why?
4. what did not go well and why?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 13.4.1 Spelling means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
5. Be able to: spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
